verdict.rationale: mise explicitly documents backward compatibility with asdf's `.tool-versions` files and can still use asdf plugins, letting asdf users adopt mise without rewriting version files, and community reviewers confirm it works as a 'drop-in asdf replacement' with better UX and confirm switching from pyenv/nvm/rbenv-style tools smoothly (mise-docs-3, mise-docs-25, mise-docs-41, mise-docs-47, mise-docs-69, mise-comm-4, mise-comm-7, mise-comm-14). Missing for 10: explicit CLI command-syntax parity with asdf (mise's own commands like `mise use`/`mise x` differ from asdf's verbs) and no first-party mapping table showing incumbent-tool command equivalents.
